title: Korean Bulgogi Grill Night
seoTitle: Korean Bulgogi Grill Night | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Marinated beef grilled with scallions and lettuce wraps for ten
subtitle: Marinated beef grilled with scallions and lettuce wraps for ten
description: Thin-sliced ribeye marinates in soy, pear, garlic, and sesame, then grills hot over charcoal or gas until caramelized at the edges. Serve with lettuce cups, scallions, kimchi, and ssamjang for wrap-your-own platters.

steps.title: Slice and marinate beef
steps.instruction: Slice ribeye paper-thin. Mix soy, grated pear, sugar, garlic, ginger, and sesame oil. Toss beef and marinate at least 1 hour.

steps.title: Prep wrap station
steps.instruction: Separate lettuce leaves, grill scallion lengths lightly, and portion kimchi and ssamjang into bowls.

steps.title: Heat the grill
steps.instruction: Preheat grill to high, about 450°F. Vent the kitchen—this will smoke. Target oven/smoker temperature: 450°F.

steps.title: Grill bulgogi in batches
steps.instruction: Grill beef in single layers 1–2 minutes per side until caramelized. Repeat until all beef is cooked. Target oven/smoker temperature: 450°F.

steps.title: Serve platters
steps.instruction: Pile hot beef on platters with grilled scallions. Let crews build lettuce wraps with kimchi and ssamjang.

proTips: A cast iron griddle on the grill gives better char than grates alone.
Offer steamed rice on the side for crew who skip lettuce wraps.
Toasted sesame seeds over finished beef add crunch and look pro.
tonightSpread: Bulgogi platters with lettuce cups, kimchi, and ssamjang.
Quick cucumber salad with rice vinegar.
leftovers: Beef becomes bulgogi quesadillas—different format, still works.
Chop into fried rice with kimchi for lunch shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Grill-night bulgogi feels interactive and special without the rice-bowl repetition. Crews build lettuce wraps, eat with their hands, and the sweet-salty beef disappears faster than you can restock the platter.
mealPrepNotes: Freeze beef 30 minutes for easier slicing. Marinate up to 8 hours. Grill in batches over highest heat—crowding steams instead of chars.
